chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, all together from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithammi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Munthir, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three will be punished on the Day of Resurrection: a man who lied in his dream, he will be commanded to tie a knot between two grains, and he will not be able to tie a knot between them; and a man who created images, he will be commanded to breathe into them, and he will not be able to breathe into them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for lying in dreams and creating images in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking the sin of false dreamers and image-makers to the concept of *tasyir* (imitating creation), a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding the prohibition of statues. The eschatological punishment of performing an impossible task—such as tying a knot between two grains or breathing life into an inanimate object—serves as a metaphor for the futility of their claim to creative power. This narration is frequently cited in discussions on the spiritual consequences of visual arts and the preservation of divine uniqueness (*Tawhid*).
